$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. ExecutionHandle per FB-RAT-EXE-001. Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<ExecutionHandle> (see schemas/common/envelope.schema.json). `handleId` is this object's own FB-RAT-COM-002 stable ID.
title: ExecutionHandle
description: Live/in-flight handle to a started ExecutionRequest: state, heartbeat, declared cancellation semantics, and (when applicable) a reconnect token. Structurally operationalizes FB-RAT-EXE-002 (lifecycle), FB-RAT-EXE-003 (every provider declares cancellation semantics + reports what is known to have stopped), FB-RAT-EXE-004 (reconnect uncertainty MUST report UNKNOWN rather than false termination or success), and FB-RAT-EXE-005 (Android recovery posture — assume the process may die; journal work; support resume/restart/explicit migration). See docs/ratified/EXECUTION_CONTRACT.md §2 for the full lifecycle transition table this `state` enum encodes.

handleId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this handle (FB-RAT-COM-002). A resumed/migrated handle after process death (FB-RAT-EXE-005) gets a NEW handleId — see `resumedFromHandleId` for the link back, rather than reusing the old id, because the old handle's last-known state remains a distinct historical fact even if it turns out to have been wrong (e.g. TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN that a resume later resolves).

requestId.description: References the ExecutionRequest.id (schemas/execution/request.schema.json) this handle was started from.

targetId.description: References the ExecutionTarget.id (schemas/execution/target.schema.json) this handle is running (or ran) on.

stateReason.description: Free-text reason for the current state, mirroring core-engine's GraphRunner.stoppedBecause pattern (WP-0 survey §1(d)) — e.g. 'budget:wallClock', 'user cancelled', 'host key changed, awaiting trust decision', 'reconnect: token stale'. Required non-null whenever `state` is one of the terminal-or-uncertain states (see the if/then below) — FB-RAT-COM-009 accessibility: this is the textual-semantics carrier for a state that is not plain success, so it must stand on its own without relying on color/icon.

enteredStateAtUtc.description: UTC instant this handle entered its current `state` (FB-RAT-COM-004).

lastHeartbeatUtc.description: UTC instant of the last confirmed liveness signal from the provider for this handle. Null before the first heartbeat arrives. A reader MUST treat a stale `lastHeartbeatUtc` (older than a few multiples of `heartbeatIntervalSeconds`) as grounds to attempt `reconnect()`, not as grounds to assume success or failure either way — the process may simply have been SIGKILLed by the Android 12+ phantom-process killer (platform grounding) with no chance to report anything.

heartbeatIntervalSeconds.description: Expected interval between heartbeats, or null if this provider/target does not support heartbeating (e.g. a CI_PIPELINE target where liveness is polled via the provider's own status API instead).

missedConsecutive.description: Count of consecutive expected heartbeats that did not arrive. Null when heartbeating is not supported for this target.

cancellationMode.description: FB-RAT-EXE-003: every provider declares cancellation semantics up front. COOPERATIVE: the running operation is signaled and given a chance to wind down cleanly (e.g. SIGTERM, a graph-run cancellation flag). FORCEFUL: the provider can only hard-stop (e.g. SIGKILL, revoke a CI run token) with no cleanup guarantee. UNSUPPORTED: this provider/operation combination cannot be cancelled once started (e.g. an already-dispatched CI Actions run past its cancel window) — a caller MUST be told this BEFORE relying on cancel() rather than discovering it via a failed cancel() call.

knownStoppedDescription.description: FB-RAT-EXE-003: what is known to have stopped, populated once a cancellation has been attempted (or the terminal state is CANCELLED). Null before any cancellation attempt. This is deliberately separate from `stateReason` — `stateReason` explains WHY the state is what it is, this field records WHAT the provider actually confirmed stopped (which may be partial, e.g. 'local process terminated; remote git push in flight at cancel time — outcome unknown').

reconnectToken.description: Opaque token a caller passes to ExecutionProvider.reconnect() to re-attach to this handle's underlying work after the requesting process/session died and restarted (FB-RAT-EXE-005). Null once the handle reaches a terminal state with no further reconnect possible, or for providers/operations where reconnect is not meaningful.

reconnectAttempt.description: Record of the most recent reconnect() attempt against this handle (or its predecessor, if this handle was itself produced by a successful reconnect — see `resumedFromHandleId`), when one has occurred. Null if no reconnect has been attempted yet.

resumedFromHandleId.description: FB-RAT-EXE-005 (support resume/restart/explicit migration): when this handle was produced by resuming journaled work after the prior handle's owning process died, this is that prior handle's handleId. Null for a handle that was not resumed from anything.

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

allOf.$comment: FB-RAT-COM-009 accessibility: a non-plain-success state MUST carry a textual-semantics reason, not rely on the enum value alone (which a display surface might render as color/icon only).

FB-RAT-EXE-004: if reconnect cannot establish state, the handle MUST report TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN, never a termination or success state. See fixtures/execution/invalid/handle-stale-token-false-success-rejected.invalid.json (violates this) and fixtures/execution/valid/handle-reconnect-stale-token-unknown.json (complies).

ExecutionState.description: FB-RAT-EXE-002 lifecycle. Non-terminal: QUEUED, PREPARING, RUNNING, WAITING_USER, SUSPENDED, VERIFYING. Terminal: SUCCEEDED, SUCCEEDED_UNVERIFIED, FAILED_SAFE, FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE, TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN, CANCELLED. See docs/ratified/EXECUTION_CONTRACT.md §2 for the full from-state/trigger/to-state/receipt table — this schema enumerates the valid values but (being a single-snapshot schema) cannot itself enforce that a given transition between two handle snapshots was a legal edge in that table; that is a provider-side state-machine obligation, mirrored in the Kotlin sealed-interface encoding in contracts/kotlin/ExecutionContracts.kt.

token.description: Opaque reconnect token. Never a secret value in the FB-RAT-EXE-007 sense (it authorizes re-attaching to already-authorized work, it does not itself grant new authority) but MUST still never be logged in plaintext alongside PII, per general log-hygiene practice.

expiresAtUtc.description: Null means no explicit expiry was set by the provider — callers MUST NOT assume that means the token is valid forever; providers SHOULD set a real expiry.

outcome.description: ESTABLISHED: reconnect succeeded and current handle state reflects confirmed target state. The three *_UNKNOWN outcomes are FB-RAT-EXE-004's 'cannot establish state' cases — each one forces `state: TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN` via the top-level if/then, never a success or clean-termination state.
